issues.title: Incorrect tauri version in metadata file
issues.description: The metadata-v2.json file specifies tauri version as "2.8.2" but the actual tauri crate version is "2.8.3" as shown in crates/tauri/Cargo.toml. This version mismatch will cause the CLI to report incorrect version information to tools and scripts that depend on this metadata. The PR updated the tauri version to 2.8.3, but the metadata file was not updated accordingly, creating an inconsistency between the actual library version and the advertised version.

issues.title: Dependency version mismatch for tauri-bundler
issues.description: The tauri-cli Cargo.toml declares a dependency on tauri-bundler version "2.6.0", but the actual tauri-bundler crate version is "2.6.1" as specified in crates/tauri-bundler/Cargo.toml. This creates a version constraint mismatch that could cause build failures or prevent the CLI from using the updated bundler with the bug fix for 32-bit Windows builds. The CHANGELOG indicates this version should have been updated to 2.6.1 to pick up the binary patching fix.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #14070 - Apply Version Updates From Current Changes
pr.author: tomerqodo

structured_output.summary:
This is a release-bookkeeping PR. It consumes two change files (binary patching fix for tauri-bundler 2.6.1, WebView2 FixedRuntime fix for tauri 2.8.3) and bumps versions across tauri-bundler, tauri-cli, tauri, and @tauri-apps/cli, along with changelogs, Cargo.lock, the generated config schema ids, and metadata-v2.json. The core bump work is consistent: the crate versions, package.json, schema $id, and changelog entries agree with each other.

The head commit (09a3ae3, "update pr") is the problem. It reverts the `tauri` entry in `crates/tauri-cli/metadata-v2.json` from `2.8.3` back to `2.8.2`, which contradicts the version bump in `crates/tauri/Cargo.toml` and the `config.schema.json` `$id`. `metadata-v2.json` is the file the CLI reads for version-pinned output, so this is a real regression, not a cosmetic one. The same head commit also adds an unrelated `homepage` field to tauri-bundler and bumps tauri-cli's Cargo.toml, which is not what a version-bump PR should contain. The lockfile also picks up transitive windows-sys/windows-targets changes that no change file or changelog mentions.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The stale `tauri` entry in metadata-v2.json is a correctness regression introduced by the head commit: the generator output said 2.8.3, and the PR overwrote it with 2.8.2, so the CLI's version metadata now disagrees with the crate it ships alongside. It's a one-line fix. The remaining items (unrelated homepage field, lockfile drift, pinned dependency range) are small cleanups that should be settled before merge but don't block the release itself.

architecture.overview:
Tauri releases are driven by covector change files in `.changes/`. Each file declares a bump type (for example `tauri-bundler: patch:bug`) and a description. The covector version step consumes these, bumps `Cargo.toml` and `package.json` versions, prepends per-crate CHANGELOG.md sections, and updates derived artifacts. Those derived artifacts include `Cargo.lock`, the generated `config.schema.json` (whose `$id` embeds the tauri version), and `crates/tauri-cli/metadata-v2.json`. That metadata file is `include_str!`-ed by the CLI in `init.rs` and `info/mod.rs`, and `.scripts/ci/sync-cli-metadata.js` is the script that keeps it in step with bumps.

This PR is the output of that version step. It deletes the two consumed change files, bumps tauri-bundler to 2.6.1, tauri to 2.8.3, tauri-cli to 2.8.1, and @tauri-apps/cli to 2.8.2, and writes the matching changelog sections. The head commit then hand-edits `metadata-v2.json` and adds a `homepage` field, which departs from what the release tooling would produce.
steps: Entry point: `.changes/*.md` change files declare bump type and summary. The two files in this PR (`binary-patching-32-bit.md`, `fix-webview2-path-timing.md`) are deleted because they've been consumed.

Version step: each affected crate's `Cargo.toml` (or `packages/cli/package.json`) gets its new version, and a `## \[x.y.z]` section is prepended to its CHANGELOG.md. The commit links every entry to its PR and author.

Derived artifacts: `Cargo.lock` gets matching `version` lines for the bumped workspace crates. `config.schema.json` (in both `crates/tauri-cli` and `crates/tauri-schema-generator/schemas`) gets the new `$id`. `metadata-v2.json` records versions the CLI reports and embeds in generated projects.

Where the head commit diverges: `metadata-v2.json` `tauri` is reverted to 2.8.2, while the generated schema and the tauri crate are at 2.8.3. A `homepage` field is also added to tauri-bundler, which is unrelated to the release.
Runtime consumers: `tauri init` and `tauri info` read `metadata-v2.json` at compile time, so the `tauri` value flows into CLI output and project scaffolding.

findings.title: metadata-v2.json reverts tauri version to 2.8.2 while the release is 2.8.3
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/metadata-v2.json`, the `"tauri"` field is `2.8.2`, but this release bumps the tauri crate to `2.8.3` (see `crates/tauri/Cargo.toml` and the `$id` in `crates/tauri-cli/config.schema.json`). Set `"tauri"` back to `"2.8.3"`. Leave the `cli.js` and `tauri-build`/`tauri-plugin` fields alone. Do not hand-edit other files; this value is consumed via `include_str!` in `crates/tauri-cli/src/init.rs` and `info/mod.rs`.

findings.title: Unrelated `homepage` field added to tauri-bundler manifest
findings.body:
The head commit adds `homepage = "https://tauri.app/"` to `crates/tauri-bundler/Cargo.toml`. It's harmless, but it isn't a version bump and has no change file or changelog entry. A release PR should carry only the release. If the field is wanted, it belongs in its own PR so it gets reviewed and noted.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-bundler/Cargo.toml" lines="9-13"}
findings.fixPrompt: Remove the `homepage = "https://tauri.app/"` line that was added to `crates/tauri-bundler/Cargo.toml` in this version-bump PR. If the homepage metadata is desired, open it as a separate change with its own change file. Keep the `version = "2.6.1"` bump.

findings.title: Lockfile transitive windows-sys/windows-targets bumps not explained by the release
findings.fixPrompt: In `Cargo.lock`, the `colored` 2.2.0, `libloading` 0.8.6, and `winapi-util` 0.1.9 entries now reference `windows-sys 0.59.0` / `windows-targets 0.52.6` where the base had `0.48.0` / `0.48.5`. Those dependency crates did not change version in this release. Check on the base commit with `cargo tree` whether these edges are required, then regenerate the lockfile so only the workspace crate versions (tauri-bundler 2.6.1, tauri 2.8.3, tauri-cli 2.8.1) change. If the re-resolution is intentional, note it in the release changelog.

findings.title: tauri-cli still pins tauri-bundler to 2.6.0 despite the changelog claiming 2.6.1
findings.body:
`crates/tauri-cli/CHANGELOG.md` says `Upgraded to tauri-bundler@2.6.1`, and the tauri-cli version is bumped to 2.8.1. But `crates/tauri-cli/Cargo.toml` still declares `tauri-bundler = { version = "2.6.0", ..., path = "../tauri-bundler" }`. The caret requirement still resolves to 2.6.1 for local builds, so nothing breaks today. For a published crate, though, the dependency requirement is what crates.io consumers see. If the intent is a minimum of the new release, the requirement should be `2.6.1`.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-cli/Cargo.toml" lines="49-51"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-cli/Cargo.toml`, the `tauri-bundler` dependency (line ~50) still says `version = "2.6.0"`, but this release upgrades it to 2.6.1 as stated in `crates/tauri-cli/CHANGELOG.md`. Update the version requirement to `"2.6.1"` so the published tauri-cli requires the release that contains the binary-patching fix. Keep the `path` and feature settings unchanged.

findings.title: Changelog contributor links are malformed (pre-existing pattern)
findings.body:
The new `by @user` links in the changelogs point at paths like `https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/../../Legend-Master`. These are relative paths appended to the repo URL, so they don't resolve to the author's profile. The same pattern appears in older entries in these files, so this PR didn't introduce it. It's worth fixing in the changelog generator rather than by hand here.

::diff{file="crates/tauri-bundler/CHANGELOG.md" lines="3-8"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `crates/tauri-bundler/CHANGELOG.md` (and `crates/tauri/CHANGELOG.md`, `crates/tauri-cli/CHANGELOG.md`, `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md`), the new `by [@user](...)` links use a broken relative URL like `https://www.github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/../../Legend-Master`. Change them to `https://github.com/<user>` form. Keep the rest of the entry unchanged. Note the same pattern exists in older entries, so consider fixing it in the changelog generator instead of editing by hand.

findings.title: Version bumps and changelogs are consistent across manifests
findings.body: The consumed change files are removed, and each bump matches its changelog section. `crates/tauri/Cargo.toml` is 2.8.3, the schema `$id` (in both `config.schema.json` copies) is 2.8.3, `packages/cli/package.json` is 2.8.2 with a changelog entry for `tauri-cli@2.8.1`, and the `Cargo.lock` workspace version lines match the manifests. The release-artifact set is complete apart from the `metadata-v2.json` regression noted above.
